result.title: ReCAP: Sequential Concept Acquisition with Guarantees under Imperfect Concept Predictors
result.summary: Sequential concept acquisition enables interpretable diagnosis from a compact set of human-understandable findings. Such explanations are useful only if clinicians can trust them, yet most existing methods treat predicted concepts as correct, so a correct diagnosis can rest on incorrectly predicted evidence. We propose Reliable Concept Acquisition with Pruning (ReCAP), which reasons over what the concept predictor reports, including errors and abstentions, and replaces conditional information gain with a label-discriminating objective that separates cases requiring different diagnoses. We prove this objective adaptively monotone and adaptively submodular, yielding a (1-1/e) guarantee for greedy fixed-budget acquisition that degrades boundedly under learned estimates, and combine it with abstention-aware acquisition and diagnosis-preserving pruning to keep explanations short and reliable. Across five medical imaging datasets, ReCAP reduces the share of correct diagnoses supported by at least one incorrectly predicted concept from 27.1% to 9.6% relative to the strongest baseline, while using fewer than half as many concepts and achieving higher diagnostic accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ReCAP，在概念预测器会出错或弃权的前提下序贯获取概念：用区分不同诊断的标签判别目标替代条件信息增益，证明其自适应单调与子模性从而给出贪心固定预算的 (1-1/e) 保证，并结合弃权感知获取与保留诊断的剪枝，在五个医学影像数据集上以更少概念提升诊断可靠性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其预算受限的序贯证据获取、弃权处理与带保证的剪枝目标，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选和 LOOK/STOP 决策提供可核查的方法线索，但研究对象是可解释概念分类而非 latent 推理状态，迁移性需核查。
